name: Apple
storageTips: Store in the crisper drawer in a plastic bag with holes for air circulation
Keep away from other produce — apples are heavy ethylene producers
Separate any bruised apples to prevent spoilage from spreading
Wash only when ready to eat
ripeTip: A ripe apple is firm with no soft spots and has a sweet fragrance near the stem.
noBenefitReason: Apples are the biggest ethylene source in the fridge, not a victim of it — and they out-gas any sachet. Store them apart from everything else instead.

name: Avocado
storageTips: Leave on the counter to ripen, then move to the refrigerator
To speed ripening, place in a paper bag with a banana
Once ripe, refrigerate to slow further ripening
Store cut avocado with the pit in, sprinkled with lemon juice, wrapped tightly
krispBenefit: A Krisp helps a little here. Once ripe and chilled, slows it going from ripe to overripe. Expect about 2–3 extra days once it is ripe and in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Gently squeeze — a ripe avocado yields to firm pressure without being mushy. The skin darkens when ripe.

name: Banana
storageTips: Keep on the counter at room temperature — never refrigerate unripe bananas
Wrap the stem in plastic wrap to slow ethylene release and extend freshness
Separate from the bunch to slow ripening
Only refrigerate if very ripe and you need to buy a couple extra days — the peel will brown but the fruit stays good
ripeTip: Yellow with small brown speckles means peak sweetness. Green tips mean it needs another day or two.
noBenefitReason: Bananas belong on the counter, and a Krisp works inside the closed crisper drawer, so it can't reach them. Keep bananas away from your other produce instead. They give off ethylene too.

name: Blueberry
storageTips: Do not wash until ready to eat — moisture promotes mold
Store in a single layer on a paper towel-lined container
Keep in the coldest part of the refrigerator
Remove any moldy berries immediately
ripeTip: Look for firm, plump berries with a uniform deep blue color and a silvery frost coating.
noBenefitReason: Berries barely react to ethylene. Mold is what ends them, so keep them dry and rinse just before eating.

name: Cantaloupe
storageTips: Store whole melon on the counter until ripe
Once ripe, refrigerate immediately
Cut melon should be wrapped and stored in the fridge for up to 3 days
Keep away from ethylene-sensitive produce
ripeTip: Ripe cantaloupe has a sweet fragrance at the stem end and yields slightly to pressure. The skin should have a golden undertone.
noBenefitReason: Whole melons ripen on the counter and are too big for the drawer. Once cut, wrap it and eat it within a few days.

name: Cherry
storageTips: Store unwashed in a breathable bag or container
Keep stems attached until ready to eat
Do not stack too deep — they bruise easily
Bring to room temperature before eating for best flavor
ripeTip: Firm, glossy, and deeply colored with green stems still attached.
noBenefitReason: Tested directly: continuous ethylene had no effect on sweet cherries in cold storage.

name: Grape
storageTips: Store unwashed in their original ventilated bag or container
Keep in the back of the fridge where it's coldest
Do not seal in an airtight container
Wash only before eating
ripeTip: Plump, firmly attached to the stem, with a powdery bloom on the skin.
noBenefitReason: Tested directly: continuous ethylene had no effect on table grapes in cold storage.

name: Kiwi
storageTips: Store unripe kiwi at room temperature until soft
Once ripe, move to the refrigerator
Keep away from ethylene-producing fruits until ready to ripen
Place near apples or bananas to speed ripening
krispBenefit: A Krisp makes a real difference here. Ripe kiwi turns mushy fast around ethylene. This slows the softening. Expect about 2–4 extra days once it is ripe and in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: A ripe kiwi yields to gentle pressure, similar to a ripe pear.

name: Lemon
storageTips: Store in the refrigerator in a sealed bag to prevent drying out
Can be left on the counter for about a week
Zest before juicing for maximum use
Store cut lemons face-down on a plate or in a sealed container
ripeTip: Choose bright yellow, firm lemons that feel heavy for their size.
noBenefitReason: Ethylene de-greens lemons rather than spoiling them, and the baseline life is already months.

name: Lime
storageTips: Store in the refrigerator in a sealed plastic bag
Keeps about a week on the counter
Microwave for 10 seconds before juicing to get more juice
Store cut limes tightly wrapped
ripeTip: Firm with glossy, bright green skin. Heavier limes have more juice.
noBenefitReason: Long baseline life and little ethylene response.

name: Mango
storageTips: Ripen on the counter at room temperature
Once ripe, refrigerate to extend freshness by several days
To speed ripening, place in a paper bag
Store cut mango in an airtight container in the fridge
ripeTip: A ripe mango gives slightly when squeezed and has a fruity aroma at the stem end. Color is not a reliable indicator.
noBenefitReason: Mangoes ripen on the counter, and once ripe they have only a day or two. A Krisp adds little.

name: Orange
storageTips: Store in the refrigerator for maximum freshness
Can sit on the counter for about a week
Do not store in sealed plastic bags — they need some air
Keep away from high ethylene producers
ripeTip: Choose oranges that are firm, heavy for their size, and have smooth skin.
noBenefitReason: Citrus barely reacts to ethylene, so a Krisp won't change much. It keeps for weeks in the fridge anyway.

name: Peach
storageTips: Ripen on the counter at room temperature, stem side down
Once slightly soft, move to the refrigerator
Store in a single layer to prevent bruising
Do not store in a sealed bag until ripe
ripeTip: A ripe peach has a sweet fragrance, yields to gentle pressure, and has creamy yellow or warm undertones (not green).
noBenefitReason: Peaches ripen on the counter, and once ripe they have only a day or two. A Krisp adds little.

name: Pear
storageTips: Pears ripen from the inside out — check the neck near the stem
Ripen on the counter, then refrigerate
Unripe pears can last months in the fridge
Keep away from strong-smelling foods
krispBenefit: A Krisp helps a little here. Once ripe and chilled, slows it going soft and mealy. Expect about 1–2 extra days once it is ripe and in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Press gently near the stem. If it yields, it's ripe. Pears ripen from the inside out, so don't wait until they feel soft all over.

name: Pineapple
storageTips: Store whole in the refrigerator for up to 5 days
Pineapples do not ripen further after picking — refrigerate right away
Once cut, store in an airtight container in the fridge for 3-4 days
Store upside down briefly to distribute sweetness before cutting
ripeTip: A ripe pineapple has a sweet fragrance at the base, golden skin, and leaves pull out easily.
noBenefitReason: Pineapple does not ripen further after harvest, so there is nothing for an absorber to slow down.

name: Plum
storageTips: Ripen on the counter until slightly soft
Once ripe, refrigerate in the crisper drawer
Store in a single layer to prevent bruising
Do not wash until ready to eat
ripeTip: Slightly soft to the touch with a sweet fragrance. The skin should have a powdery bloom.
noBenefitReason: Tested directly: continuous ethylene had no effect on plums in cold storage.

name: Strawberry
storageTips: Do not wash until ready to eat — moisture causes mold
Store in a single layer on paper towels
Remove any moldy berries immediately
Keep stems on until eating
ripeTip: Bright red all the way to the stem with a sweet aroma. Avoid berries with white or green tips.
noBenefitReason: Berries barely react to ethylene. Mold is what ends them, so keep them dry and rinse just before eating.

name: Tomato
storageTips: Store stem-side down on the counter at room temperature
Never refrigerate unripe tomatoes — cold kills flavor and texture
Only refrigerate if very ripe and you need to buy time
Keep away from direct sunlight
ripeTip: Slightly soft, uniformly colored, and fragrant at the stem end.
noBenefitReason: Tomatoes keep their flavor best on the counter, out of reach of a Krisp in the drawer. If you move ripe ones into the fridge to hold them a couple more days, a Krisp in that drawer helps a little.

name: Watermelon
storageTips: Store whole watermelon on the counter until cut
Once cut, wrap tightly and refrigerate
Keep away from ethylene-producing fruits
Whole melons keep better at cool room temperature than in the fridge
ripeTip: A ripe watermelon sounds hollow when tapped, has a creamy yellow ground spot, and feels heavy for its size.
noBenefitReason: Whole melons are too big for the drawer. Once cut, wrap it and eat it within a few days.

name: Nectarine
storageTips: Ripen at room temperature stem-side down
Once ripe, refrigerate immediately
Store in a single layer to prevent bruising
Keep away from other ethylene producers
ripeTip: Slightly soft along the seam with a fragrant aroma. Avoid green-tinged fruit.
noBenefitReason: Tested directly: continuous ethylene had no effect on nectarines in cold storage.

name: Papaya
storageTips: Ripen at room temperature until skin is mostly yellow
Refrigerate once ripe
Store cut papaya in an airtight container
Place in a paper bag with a banana to speed ripening
ripeTip: Mostly yellow to orange skin that gives slightly to pressure. A slight sweet aroma at the stem.
noBenefitReason: Papayas ripen on the counter, and once ripe they have only a day or two. A Krisp adds little.

name: Pomegranate
storageTips: Store whole in the refrigerator for up to 3 months
Arils (seeds) can be stored in an airtight container for up to 5 days
Can also sit on the counter for 1-2 weeks
Freeze arils in a single layer for long-term storage
ripeTip: Heavy for its size with a deep color. The skin should be smooth and firm.
noBenefitReason: Loss is water loss and husk scald, not ripening.

name: Asparagus
storageTips: Trim the ends and stand upright in a jar with 1 inch of water
Cover loosely with a plastic bag
Or wrap ends in a damp paper towel
Use as soon as possible for best flavor
krispBenefit: A Krisp helps a little here. Slows the spears turning tough and woody. Expect about 1–2 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Choose firm, bright green stalks with tight, compact tips.

name: Bell Pepper
storageTips: Store whole in the crisper drawer
Do not wash until ready to use
Cut peppers should be stored in an airtight container
Green peppers last longer than red, yellow, or orange
ripeTip: Firm with glossy, wrinkle-free skin and a fresh green stem.
noBenefitReason: Low ethylene sensitivity — peppers soften from water loss, not from ethylene.

name: Broccoli
storageTips: Store unwashed in a loose plastic bag in the crisper
Do not seal tightly — broccoli needs air circulation
Wrap stems in a damp paper towel
Use within a few days for best nutrition and flavor
krispBenefit: A Krisp makes a real difference here. Keeps the florets green instead of yellowing. Expect about 2–4 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Tight, dark green florets with firm stems. Avoid any yellowing.

name: Brussels Sprouts
storageTips: Store in a breathable bag in the crisper drawer
Do not wash until ready to cook
Keep on the stalk if possible for longer freshness
Remove any yellowed outer leaves before storing
krispBenefit: A Krisp makes a real difference here. Keeps the outer leaves from yellowing. Expect about 2–3 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Tight, compact heads that are bright green with no yellowing.

name: Cabbage
storageTips: Store whole in the crisper drawer
Do not cut until ready to use
Wrap cut cabbage tightly in plastic wrap
Outer leaves may wilt but protect the inner head
krispBenefit: A Krisp makes a real difference here. Slows outer leaves yellowing and loosening from the head. Expect about 2–4 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Choose heads that feel heavy and compact with crisp, tightly packed leaves.

name: Carrot
storageTips: Remove green tops before storing — they draw moisture
Store in a plastic bag in the crisper drawer
Can be stored in water in the fridge for extra crispness
Keep away from ethylene-producing fruits to prevent bitterness
krispBenefit: A Krisp makes a real difference here. Helps keep carrots from picking up a bitter taste from ethylene. Expect about 2–3 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Firm, smooth, and bright orange. Avoid carrots that bend or have cracks.

name: Cauliflower
storageTips: Store stem-side up in a loose bag in the crisper
Do not wash until ready to cook
Wrap in a damp paper towel inside a bag
Brown spots can be trimmed — the rest is still good
krispBenefit: A Krisp makes a real difference here. Slows browning on the head and yellowing leaves. Expect about 2–3 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Compact, creamy white heads with no dark spots. Leaves should be green and fresh.

name: Celery
storageTips: Wrap in aluminum foil to hold in moisture
Store whole in the crisper drawer
Cut celery can be stored in water to keep crisp
Keep away from ethylene producers
ripeTip: Firm, crisp stalks that snap when bent. Look for bright green color and fresh leaves.
noBenefitReason: Celery only loses its green at high ethylene levels and warm temperatures, well beyond a cold crisper drawer. It mostly fails by drying out, so wrapping it does more than a Krisp.

name: Corn
storageTips: Keep in the husk until ready to cook
Refrigerate immediately — corn loses sweetness rapidly
Use as soon as possible after purchase
Store in the crisper drawer without removing silk
ripeTip: Look for bright green, tightly wrapped husks with moist silk. Kernels should be plump when peeked.
noBenefitReason: Sweet corn loses its sugar to starch conversion, which is a temperature problem. Chill it fast instead.

name: Cucumber
storageTips: Store in the warmest part of the fridge (door or front)
Wrap individually in a paper towel, then loosely in a bag
Cucumbers are sensitive to cold — too cold causes water-soaked spots
Keep away from ethylene-producing fruits
krispBenefit: A Krisp makes a real difference here. Slows yellowing and soft, watery spots. Expect about 2–3 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Firm, dark green, and medium-sized. Avoid soft spots or yellowing.

name: Eggplant
storageTips: Store in the crisper drawer without a bag for air circulation
Use within a few days for best quality
Sensitive to cold — keep in the warmer part of the fridge
Do not cut until ready to cook to prevent browning
krispBenefit: A Krisp helps a little here. Slows browning at the cap and softening. Expect about 1–2 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Firm with smooth, glossy, deep purple skin. Should feel heavy for its size.

name: Garlic
storageTips: Store in a cool, dark, dry place with good ventilation
Do not refrigerate whole bulbs — moisture causes sprouting
Keep in a mesh bag or open container
Once broken from the bulb, use cloves within 10 days
ripeTip: Firm bulbs with tight, papery skin. Avoid soft, sprouting, or shriveled cloves.
noBenefitReason: Garlic is a dry pantry item at 65–70% humidity. Sprouting and damp are what get it, not ethylene.

name: Green Beans
storageTips: Store unwashed in a breathable bag in the crisper
Do not snap or trim until ready to cook
Keep away from ethylene-producing fruits
Blanch and freeze for long-term storage
krispBenefit: A Krisp helps a little here. Slows yellowing and browning. Expect about 2–3 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Firm, bright green, and snap cleanly when bent. Avoid limp or spotted beans.

name: Kale
storageTips: Store unwashed in a plastic bag with some air
Wrap in a damp paper towel to maintain moisture
Remove any yellowed or wilted leaves
Can be blanched and frozen for months
krispBenefit: A Krisp makes a real difference here. Slows the leaves yellowing. Expect about 2–3 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Dark green, firm leaves with no yellowing or wilting. Smaller leaves are more tender.

name: Lettuce
storageTips: Store unwashed in a bag lined with paper towels
Keep in the crisper drawer on the humid setting
Remove damaged outer leaves to prevent spreading decay
Never store near apples, pears, or bananas
krispBenefit: A Krisp makes a real difference here. Slows russet spotting, the brown specks on romaine and leaf lettuce. Expect about 2–4 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Crisp, vibrant leaves with no browning or slimy spots.

name: Mushroom
storageTips: Store in a paper bag — never in plastic (traps moisture)
Do not wash until ready to cook
Keep in the main section of the fridge, not the crisper
Clean with a damp cloth or brush instead of rinsing
ripeTip: Firm, dry, and evenly colored. Avoid slimy or darkened mushrooms.
noBenefitReason: The one head-to-head trial of an ethylene absorber in mushroom packaging found no difference in shelf life.

name: Onion
storageTips: Store in a cool, dark, dry, well-ventilated area
Keep away from potatoes — they cause each other to spoil faster
Do not store in the refrigerator until cut
Cut onions should be refrigerated in an airtight container
ripeTip: Firm with dry, papery outer skin and no soft spots or sprouting.
noBenefitReason: Onions are a dry pantry item, and ethylene actually suppresses sprouting rather than causing it — it is sold commercially as a sprout inhibitor.

name: Peas
storageTips: Refrigerate immediately — peas lose sweetness fast
Store in a perforated bag in the crisper
Do not shell until ready to eat or cook
Blanch and freeze for long-term storage
krispBenefit: A Krisp helps a little here. Slows the pods yellowing. Expect about 1–2 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Bright green, plump pods that are firm to the touch.

name: Potato
storageTips: Store in a cool, dark, well-ventilated area (not the refrigerator)
Keep in a paper bag, basket, or open container
Never store with onions — they release gases that cause sprouting
Avoid exposure to light which causes greening
ripeTip: Firm with no green spots, sprouts, or soft areas.
noBenefitReason: The research genuinely disagrees here — some studies show ethylene breaking dormancy, others show it suppressing sprouts. Cool, dark and ventilated is what matters.

name: Spinach
storageTips: Store in a container lined with paper towels
Do not wash until ready to use
Remove any slimy or wilted leaves
Keep away from ethylene-producing fruits
krispBenefit: A Krisp makes a real difference here. Slows the leaves yellowing. Expect about 2–3 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Bright, deep green leaves that are crisp and dry with no slimy or yellow patches.

name: Sweet Potato
storageTips: Store in a cool, dark, well-ventilated area
Do not refrigerate — cold temperatures alter texture and flavor
Keep away from heat sources
Use within a month for best quality
ripeTip: Firm with smooth, even-colored skin and no cracks or soft spots.
noBenefitReason: A pantry item that should not be refrigerated at all.

name: Zucchini
storageTips: Store in a plastic bag in the crisper drawer
Do not wash until ready to cook
Keep away from ethylene producers
Can be stored at cool room temperature for a few days
krispBenefit: A Krisp helps a little here. Slows yellowing and soft spots. Expect about 1–2 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Small to medium-sized with firm, glossy, dark green skin.

name: Herbs (Fresh)
storageTips: Treat tender herbs (cilantro, parsley, basil) like flowers — trim stems and place in a glass of water
Cover loosely with a bag and refrigerate (except basil — keep on the counter)
Wrap hardy herbs (rosemary, thyme) in a damp paper towel, then seal in a bag
Do not wash until ready to use
ripeTip: Bright, vibrant color with a strong aroma and no wilting or dark spots.
noBenefitReason: In a jar on the shelf, herbs are out of the Krisp's reach. Bagged in the high-humidity drawer instead, the Krisp helps keep them from yellowing.

name: Radish
storageTips: Remove greens before storing — they draw moisture
Store in a plastic bag in the crisper drawer
Keep in water for extra crispness
Greens can be stored separately and used within a day or two
ripeTip: Firm with smooth, brightly colored skin and fresh-looking greens.
noBenefitReason: The roots are not ethylene-sensitive; the tops are. Twist the tops off and the problem goes away.

name: Squash (Winter)
storageTips: Store in a cool, dark, dry place with good ventilation
Do not refrigerate whole squash
Once cut, wrap and refrigerate for up to 5 days
Keep each squash from touching to prevent rot from spreading
ripeTip: Hard skin that can't be dented with a fingernail, heavy for its size, with a dry, corky stem.
noBenefitReason: Winter squash keeps for months in a cool pantry, well away from the fridge.

name: Grapefruit
storageTips: Store in the refrigerator for longest freshness
Can sit on the counter for about a week
No special storage requirements — quite hardy
Bring to room temperature before eating for best flavor
ripeTip: Heavy for its size with thin, smooth skin. Color does not indicate ripeness.
noBenefitReason: Citrus is only moderately sensitive and keeps for weeks regardless — ethylene changes the peel colour rather than the fruit inside.

name: Apricot
storageTips: Ripen at room temperature until slightly soft
Once ripe, refrigerate immediately
Store in a single layer to prevent bruising
Handle gently — they bruise very easily
ripeTip: Slightly soft to the touch with a deep golden-orange color and a sweet fragrance.
noBenefitReason: Stone fruit showed no measurable response to ethylene over three to eight weeks of cold storage.

name: Honeydew
storageTips: Store whole melon on the counter until ripe
Once ripe, refrigerate whole or cut
Wrap cut melon tightly in plastic
Keep away from ethylene-producing fruits
ripeTip: Slightly waxy feel, creamy yellow skin (not white), and a faint sweet smell at the blossom end.
noBenefitReason: Whole melons ripen on the counter and are too big for the drawer. Once cut, wrap it and eat it within a few days.

name: Raspberry
storageTips: Do not wash until ready to eat — moisture causes mold rapidly
Store in a single layer on a paper towel-lined container
Remove any moldy berries immediately to prevent spreading
Keep in the coldest part of the refrigerator
ripeTip: Plump, deeply colored, and easily pulls from the stem. Avoid berries with visible mold or juice staining the container.
noBenefitReason: Grey mould, not ethylene, is what ends a raspberry.

name: Blackberry
storageTips: Do not wash until ready to eat — moisture promotes rapid mold growth
Spread in a single layer on paper towels in a shallow container
Remove any crushed or moldy berries immediately
Eat as soon as possible — blackberries are very perishable
ripeTip: Deep black color, plump, and slightly soft. Red or purple berries are underripe and will be tart.
noBenefitReason: Berries fail to mould and water loss, not ethylene.

name: Jalapeño
storageTips: Store whole in a paper bag or loosely wrapped in the crisper drawer
Do not wash until ready to use
Cut peppers should be stored in an airtight container
Freeze whole for long-term storage — texture changes but flavor is preserved
ripeTip: Firm with smooth, glossy skin. Red jalapeños are riper and slightly sweeter than green ones.
noBenefitReason: Chiles respond to ethylene only mildly, and they give way to water loss and soft spots long before ripening gas becomes the problem.

name: Cranberry
storageTips: Store in their original bag in the refrigerator
Remove any soft or discolored berries
Do not wash until ready to use
Freeze for up to a year — they freeze exceptionally well
ripeTip: Firm, plump, and deep red. They should bounce when dropped — soft berries are past their prime.
noBenefitReason: Low ethylene sensitivity and a long baseline life.

name: Fig
storageTips: Store in a single layer on a paper towel-lined plate
Refrigerate immediately — figs are extremely perishable
Bring to room temperature before eating for best flavor
Do not stack or they will bruise and spoil quickly
ripeTip: Slightly soft to the touch with a sweet fragrance. The skin may have small cracks near the base when perfectly ripe.
noBenefitReason: Low sensitivity, and figs already give off a fair amount of ethylene themselves.

name: Green Onion
storageTips: Stand upright in a jar with an inch of water and cover loosely with a bag
Change the water every few days
Alternatively, wrap in a damp paper towel and place in a bag
Trim and freeze for long-term storage
ripeTip: Firm white bulbs with crisp, bright green tops. Avoid any with slimy or yellowed greens.
noBenefitReason: Green onions don't react to ethylene from other produce. Warmth and age are what yellow the tops, so keeping them cold and damp does more than a Krisp.

name: Mandarin
storageTips: Refrigerate loose in the crisper drawer if you will not eat them within a few days
Take them out of the mesh bag or box so one moldy fruit does not spread to the rest
A few days in a fruit bowl is fine for the ones you will eat first
Check every few days and remove any soft or moldy fruit
ripeTip: Heavy for their size with glossy, deep orange skin. A slightly loose peel is normal. Soft spots or a musty smell are not.
noBenefitReason: Citrus reacts only mildly to ethylene, and mold is what usually ends mandarins. A Krisp won't change much.

name: Cilantro
storageTips: Trim the stems and stand the bunch in a jar with an inch of water
Cover loosely with a bag and keep the jar on a fridge shelf
Change the water every couple of days
Keep the leaves dry and do not wash them until you use them
ripeTip: Bright green, perky leaves with a strong smell. Skip bunches with yellow, dark or slimy leaves.
noBenefitReason: In a jar on the shelf, cilantro is out of the Krisp's reach. Bagged in the high-humidity drawer instead, the Krisp helps keep it from yellowing.

name: Parsley
storageTips: Trim the stems and stand the bunch in a jar with an inch of water
Cover loosely with a bag and keep the jar on a fridge shelf
Change the water every couple of days
Or wrap it in a barely damp paper towel inside a bag in the crisper drawer
ripeTip: Deep green, springy leaves with firm stems. Skip bunches with yellow or wilted leaves.
noBenefitReason: In a jar on the shelf, parsley is out of the Krisp's reach. Bagged in the high-humidity drawer instead, the Krisp helps keep it from yellowing.

name: Basil
storageTips: Trim the stems and stand the bunch in a glass of water on the counter, out of direct sun
Do not refrigerate it. Basil leaves turn black in the cold
Change the water every day or two
Blend extra leaves into pesto and freeze it
ripeTip: Glossy, bright green leaves with no black spots, and a strong smell when you brush them.
noBenefitReason: Basil lives on the counter because the fridge blackens it, so it never shares a drawer with a Krisp. It barely reacts to ethylene anyway.

name: Bagged Salad
storageTips: Keep the bag or tub sealed and cold until you need it, and go by the use-by date
Once opened, eat it within about 2 days
Tuck a dry paper towel into the opened bag or tub to soak up moisture
Keep it off the back wall of the fridge, where the leaves can freeze
ripeTip: Pick the bag with the latest date, dry leaves and no dark, wet or slimy pieces.
noBenefitReason: Bagged salad is cut, washed and sealed, so it runs on its use-by date. Once the bag is open, moisture and bruised edges end it in about two days, and a Krisp won't change that.

name: Bok Choy
storageTips: Store unwashed in a loose plastic bag in the crisper drawer
Wrap it in a dry paper towel first if the leaves are damp
Keep it away from apples, pears and other ethylene producers
Wash between the stalks just before cooking, where grit hides
krispBenefit: A Krisp helps a little here. Slows the leaves yellowing. Expect about 1–2 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Firm, white or pale green stalks and dark leaves with no yellowing, holes or brown spots.

name: Collard Greens
storageTips: Store unwashed in a loose plastic bag in the crisper drawer
Wrap the bunch in a barely damp paper towel to hold in moisture
Keep them away from apples, pears and other ethylene producers
Blanch and freeze what you will not cook this week
krispBenefit: A Krisp helps a little here. Slows the leaves yellowing. Expect about 1–2 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Dark green, firm leaves with no yellow edges or slimy spots. Smaller leaves are more tender.

name: Swiss Chard
storageTips: Store unwashed in a loose plastic bag in the crisper drawer
Wrap the bunch in a barely damp paper towel to hold in moisture
Keep it away from apples, pears and other ethylene producers
Cook the stems a few minutes before the leaves. They take longer
krispBenefit: A Krisp helps a little here. Slows the leaves yellowing and browning at the edges. Expect about 1–2 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Glossy, crisp leaves and firm, brightly colored stems. Skip bunches with yellow or brown edges.

name: Arugula
storageTips: Keep it in its container or a bag with a dry paper towel to soak up moisture
Store it in the crisper drawer on the humid setting
Do not wash it until you use it
Pick out yellow or slimy leaves so they do not spoil the rest
krispBenefit: A Krisp helps a little here. Slows the leaves yellowing. Expect about 1–2 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Dry, bright green leaves with no yellow, dark or slimy pieces.

name: Mustard Greens
storageTips: Store unwashed in a loose plastic bag in the crisper drawer
Wrap the bunch in a barely damp paper towel to hold in moisture
Keep them away from apples, pears and other ethylene producers
Blanch and freeze what you will not cook this week
krispBenefit: A Krisp helps a little here. Slows the leaves yellowing. Expect about 1–2 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Crisp, bright green leaves with no yellowing or brown spots. Smaller leaves are milder.

name: Beet
storageTips: Cut the greens off an inch above the root so they stop pulling moisture out of it
Store the unwashed roots in a bag in the crisper drawer
Use the greens within 2 to 3 days. Cook them like chard
Leave the skin and root tail on until after cooking so the color does not bleed
ripeTip: Firm, smooth roots with no soft spots. If the greens are attached, they should look fresh, not wilted.
noBenefitReason: Beets barely react to ethylene. Drying out is what turns them soft, so a bag in the drawer does more than a Krisp.

name: Ginger
storageTips: Store it unpeeled in a zip bag in the crisper drawer with the air pressed out
Blot cut ends dry before you put it back
Freeze it whole for longer storage and grate it straight from the freezer
On the counter it keeps about a week before it starts to shrivel
ripeTip: Firm and heavy with smooth, taut skin. Skip pieces that are wrinkled, soft or moldy at the cut ends.
noBenefitReason: Ginger barely reacts to ethylene. It ends by shriveling or molding, so keeping it dry and bagged matters more than a Krisp.

name: Leek
storageTips: Store unwashed and untrimmed in a loose plastic bag in the crisper drawer
Keep the bag closed. Leeks pass their smell to other food
Keep them away from apples, pears and other ethylene producers
Slice them lengthwise and rinse between the layers just before cooking
krispBenefit: A Krisp helps a little here. Slows the softening ethylene causes. Expect about 1–2 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Firm, straight white stalks with crisp, dark green tops. Skip any with yellow or slimy leaves.

name: Artichoke
storageTips: Store unwashed in a plastic bag in the crisper drawer
Sprinkle a few drops of water in the bag to keep the leaves from drying out
Do not trim or cut them until you cook them. Cut surfaces brown quickly
Cook them within a week. The flavor fades the longer they sit
ripeTip: Heavy for its size with tight, squeaky leaves. A little brown on the tips is fine. Spreading, dry leaves mean it is old.
noBenefitReason: Artichokes barely react to ethylene. They dry out and bruise, so a bag in the drawer does more than a Krisp.

name: Pumpkin
storageTips: Store whole pumpkins in a cool, dry place with air moving around them
Do not refrigerate a whole pumpkin. Below 50°F the cold damages it
Keep them off bare concrete and from touching each other
Once cut, wrap it and refrigerate for up to 5 days, or cook and freeze the flesh
ripeTip: Hard skin a fingernail cannot dent, a firm stem still attached, and no soft spots. Pie or sugar pumpkins are the ones for cooking.
noBenefitReason: Whole pumpkins keep in a cool, dry spot, well away from the fridge and the Krisp.

name: Okra
storageTips: Keep the pods dry in a paper bag or a loosely closed bag
Store them in the warmest part of the fridge, like the door or the front of the crisper
Do not wash them until just before cooking. Wet pods turn slimy
Use them within 2 to 3 days, or slice and freeze them
ripeTip: Small, bright green pods, 2 to 4 inches long, that snap at the tip. Big, dull pods are tough and stringy.
noBenefitReason: Okra lasts only two or three days at home. Drying out, bruising and cold damage end it long before ethylene matters, so a Krisp won't help.

name: Plantain
storageTips: Keep them on the counter, out of direct sun. Never refrigerate green plantains
Green ones are starchy, for tostones. Yellow with black spots are sweet, for frying
To speed up ripening, put them in a paper bag
Once fully ripe, refrigerate them for a few days or peel and freeze them
ripeTip: Firm and heavy with no mold at the stem. Choose green for savory dishes and yellow to black for sweet ones.
noBenefitReason: Plantains belong on the counter, and a Krisp works inside the closed crisper drawer, so it can't reach them. Keep them away from apples and bananas if you want them to stay green.

name: Tomatillo
storageTips: Leave the husks on and store them in a paper bag in the crisper drawer
Keep them dry. Damp husks grow mold
Peel the husk and rinse off the sticky coating just before using them
On the counter they keep about a week
ripeTip: Firm, bright green fruit that fills its husk. The husk should be dry and papery, not slimy or moldy.
noBenefitReason: Ethylene can turn tomatillos yellow, but they react only mildly and there is no data to put a number on it. Dry husks and steady cold matter more.

name: Persimmon
storageTips: Keep firm, squat Fuyu persimmons in the coldest part of the fridge and eat them while they are still crisp
Ripen acorn-shaped Hachiya persimmons on the counter until they feel like jelly. They are mouth-puckering until then
Keep them away from apples, pears and bananas unless you want them to soften faster
Scoop out and freeze the pulp of very soft persimmons for baking
krispBenefit: A Krisp helps a little here. Slows firm persimmons going soft around ethylene. Expect about 1–2 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Deep orange, glossy skin with the green cap still attached. Fuyu should be firm. Hachiya should be very soft before you eat it.

name: Parsnip
storageTips: Cut off any green tops. They pull moisture out of the root
Store unwashed in a plastic bag in the crisper drawer
Keep them away from apples and pears. Ethylene makes parsnips bitter
Peel or scrub them just before cooking
krispBenefit: A Krisp helps a little here. Helps keep parsnips from picking up a bitter taste from ethylene. Expect about 1–2 extra days in a closed crisper drawer.
ripeTip: Firm, cream-colored roots, small to medium in size. Very large ones can have a woody core.

name: Turnip
storageTips: Cut off the greens so they stop pulling moisture out of the root
Store the unwashed roots in a plastic bag in the crisper drawer
Use the greens within 2 to 3 days. Cook them like mustard greens
Peel large turnips before cooking. Small ones only need a scrub
ripeTip: Small, heavy and firm with smooth skin. Large turnips can be woody and sharp-tasting.
noBenefitReason: Turnips barely react to ethylene. They go soft from drying out, so a bag in the drawer does more than a Krisp.

name: Fennel
storageTips: Cut the stalks off the bulb and store the two separately
Keep the bulb in a loose plastic bag in the crisper drawer
Use the feathery fronds within 2 to 3 days, like a fresh herb
Slice it just before using. Cut surfaces brown quickly
ripeTip: A firm, white to pale green bulb with no brown spots or splits, and fresh green fronds.
noBenefitReason: There is no published data on how fennel reacts to ethylene, so we make no Krisp claim for it. Keeping it cold and bagged is what works.
ethyleneNote: Fennel gives off only a little ethylene. There is no published data on how it reacts to ethylene from other produce, so keep it away from ripening fruit to be safe.
